join_order.notes: suppkey is dense 0-100K; use direct array for aggregation. After finding max revenue, lookup matching suppkey(s) via supplier pk index.

data_structures.thread_local_aggregation: direct_array(double, max_suppkey+1, per_thread ~800KB, allocated via calloc inside parallel region for NUMA first-touch)

indexes.condition: lookup row_id for matching suppkey(s) to retrieve s_name, s_address, s_phone

parallelism.notes: Cap threads to min(nproc, qualifying_blocks, 16). With ~34 qualifying blocks and 800KB per thread-local array, 16 threads = 12.8MB which fits comfortably in 44MB L3. Allocate thread-local arrays INSIDE the parallel region using calloc (not std::vector) for NUMA-aware first-touch and to avoid constructor overhead. Each thread calloc's its own revenue array on first use, and free's after merge.

scan_phase.merge: parallel element-wise sum of thread-local arrays into global array

execution_phases.name: zonemap_filter
execution_phases.description: Load lineitem_l_shipdate_zonemap. Build list of qualifying block indices where block overlaps [9497, 9588). Then set nthreads = min(omp_get_max_threads(), num_qualifying_blocks, 16).

execution_phases.name: parallel_scan_aggregate
execution_phases.description: Use omp_set_num_threads(nthreads). Inside #pragma omp parallel: each thread allocates its own revenue array via calloc(rev_size, sizeof(double)) — this ensures NUMA first-touch locality and avoids std::vector constructor overhead. Then #pragma omp for schedule(static) over qualifying blocks: for each block, scan l_shipdate in [shipdate_lo, shipdate_hi), accumulate revenue[l_suppkey[i]] += l_extendedprice[i] * (1.0 - l_discount[i]). After the parallel for, merge: allocate global revenue array via calloc, then #pragma omp for schedule(static) over rev_size to sum all thread-local arrays element-wise. Each thread frees its local array after merge.
execution_phases.mmap_advice: MADV_SEQUENTIAL + MADV_HUGEPAGE on all four column files, no MAP_POPULATE

execution_phases.name: find_max
execution_phases.description: Single pass over revenue[0..rev_size-1] to find max_revenue. Then collect all suppkeys where fabs(revenue[sk] - max_revenue) < 1e-6 and revenue[sk] > 0.

execution_phases.name: lookup_supplier
execution_phases.description: For each matching suppkey, use supplier_s_suppkey_lookup to get row_id. Read s_name, s_address, s_phone from supplier varlen columns at that row_id. Output sorted by s_suppkey.

mmap_strategy.resource_scoping: declare mmap resources (MmapFile structs) BEFORE the RAII timer scope so that munmap TLB shootdown cost is excluded from timing

optimization_notes: Category B+C: Root cause is 64 thread-local revenue arrays (64 × 800KB = 50MB) exceeding L3 cache (44MB), all zero-initialized sequentially in the main thread via std::vector before the parallel region — causing 50MB of serial page faults and cache thrashing. Fix: (1) Cap threads to min(nproc, qualifying_blocks, 16) — with ~34 qualifying blocks, 16 threads × 800KB = 12.8MB fits comfortably in L3. (2) Allocate thread-local arrays via calloc INSIDE the parallel region for NUMA first-touch locality, eliminating serial initialization bottleneck. (3) Use calloc instead of std::vector to avoid zero-init constructor overhead (OS provides zero pages via copy-on-write). These changes reduce memory pressure by 4× and parallelize initialization cost across threads.
